newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks show new slim loss at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks show new slim loss at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks showed a modest drop for the third session running Thursday and were likely to end the week on a soft note, dealers said.

"The market is continuing its downward correction, which should carry on tomorrow," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "Trading was very selective and several stocks were weighed down by (Friday's) options expirations."
The blue-chip MerVal index closed 0.3 percent lower at 727.76. It had shed the same amount Tuesday and Wednesday but still stands 0.3 percent higher so far in the week.
Technical analysts said the MerVal could find support at 715 between Friday and Monday.
"We don't think the market will remain subdued for very long -- the charts show the MerVal should be heading back up early next week," one analyst said.
However, traders noted the bolsa could remain weak if Wall Street extended Thursday's dive.

"The fall in the New York markets today affected us. And there's a chance the Dow may have started a significant retreat which could take it as low as 6750 -- this will hurt ADRs and keep a lid on the bolsa," Bonanno said.
The broad market index closed off 0.6 percent, with losers overtaking winners 31 to 22 and 19 issues closing flat.
Floor turnover remained brisk at 33 million pesos compared to 34.8 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter volume slowed to 62.6 million pesos from 97.2 million Wednesday.

Top main-tier risers were steelmaker Acindar, which jumped 4.3 percent, construction stock Polledo, up 1.9 percent, and Banco de Galica, up 1.3 percent. Losers were led by power firm Central Costanera, oil company Astra and pulp maker Celulosa, off 2.9 percent, 2.7 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
